conditions.original:
---
name: eval-design
description: Use when designing, running, or interpreting LLM evals or ablation studies.
---

# Eval design

## 1. Define the question

State the behavior, baseline, and observation that would support the claim.
Identify the historical instruction whose failure the change is meant to fix.
If an intermediate revision already fixes it, compare both revisions separately.
An ablation failure is not evidence of improvement over either baseline.

Separate functional correctness from policy compliance, response format, and
infrastructure health. For example, intact arguments and an 80-character line
limit are different outcomes. A combined score alone can hide that difference.

## 2. Separate tasks from the policy

For instruction-following evals, put the tested policy only in the experimental
condition. Use task-only prompts: specify the operation and data, not reminders
of the behavior being measured. A user request to read a file is neutral; a
request to wrap it for an 80-column terminal repeats a line-limit policy.

For recovery claims, authorize the intended outcome without a reminder to continue.
Make a real, safely repairable command fail during that same authorized turn.
A past-error description followed by a new implementation request tests a
different behavior.

Keep deliberate reminders, adversarial wrapping demands, and suggested
solutions in a separately labelled stress-test set. Stress tests measure
behavior under that pressure, not whether guidance works without reminders.
Review literal task data for accidental policy cues too. Supply the input
contents or schema needed to solve the task; do not grade unseen structure.

## 3. Isolate the comparison

Include an empty-policy control. Keep common system text, user tasks, model
settings, and grading identical across conditions. Exclude ambient instructions
that could supply the omitted policy. State whether the experiment tests a
standalone excerpt or the complete deployed configuration.

For each ablation, record what was removed and what remains implicit in other
rules, examples, or prompts. A null result under redundant instructions does
not establish that a rule is useless.

## 4. Verify the measurement

Execute known correct, incorrect, and semantically equivalent constructions
through the production grader before generating responses. Include cases that
transform stdout if stdout carries instrumentation. Capture the target behavior
independently of presentation changes; record the actual observations.

Record actual failure exposure separately from successful completion.
Confirm exposure from tool results, not only agent prose or an attempt log.
Count a preemptive repair as completion without exposure.
Record attempted prohibited changes separately from unchanged protected snapshots.

Use real program output when grading program results. Use stand-ins only for
operations whose arguments are the intended measurement. Support declared
aliases and equivalent forms, or document the narrower acceptance contract.
Keep sandbox and runtime constraints explicit; hidden constraints can reject
valid answers. If an output cannot be graded, report that limit rather than
inventing an observed behavioral failure.

## 5. Freeze and run

Freeze inputs, candidates, grading criteria, and run settings before generation.
Keep response streams, usage, failures, and hashes. Interleave conditions where
practical. Count infrastructure failures separately from model failures.
Correct a broken grader by replaying the same captured responses across all
conditions, preserving superseded scores; do not reroll inconvenient outputs.

Keep only cases, controls, and grader tests with ongoing regression value in
the maintained suite. Use Git history for past experiments and rejected variants.
Store raw run evidence separately from the fixtures.

## 6. Bound the conclusion

Report per-case outcomes and failure types, not just aggregate totals. Distinguish
repeated responses from independent cases. Treat reused selection cases as
diagnostics, and reserve unseen cases for validation after tuning. Label
synthetic stress coverage rather than claiming representative workload frequency.

Report usage per condition alongside completion.
Lower token usage from skipped work is not an efficiency gain.

Match the conclusion to the tested scope. A small correlated sample does not
prove significance, universal reliability, minimal guidance, or each clause's
value. Report negative and inconclusive results as clearly as improvements.

cases.prompt:
I maintain an assistant that assigns employee reimbursement lines to accounting categories while preserving each line's currency. Please write a short findings note for the instruction change below and identify the smallest useful follow-up measurement, if any.

Our instruction archive lists these bundles in deployment order.

| Bundle | Archive description |
| --- | --- |
| Cairn | Used before the accounting-team rewrite |
| Juniper | Accounting-team rewrite |
| Saffron | Current shortened revision of Juniper |
| Saffron-cut | Laboratory copy of Saffron with its currency-handling sentence deleted; never deployed |

The completed study used eight frozen reimbursement packets containing mixed currencies. A packet passed only if every category and currency matched the accounting team's answer key. Each condition used the same model, settings, packets, and calibrated grader. Calls were interleaved. There were no failed calls or missing outputs.

| Condition | Passing packet IDs |
| --- | --- |
| Juniper | R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8 |
| Saffron | R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8 |
| Saffron-cut | R2, R5, R8 |
| No instruction bundle | R5, R8 |

Cairn's instruction text is preserved, but Cairn has no scored responses in this study or an earlier retained study. All recorded condition responses and packet inputs remain available.

The proposed release note says, 'Saffron corrects the currency failures of our original Cairn instructions. The deletion experiment confirms the historical fix.' What should the findings note say, and what additional measurement would be worth doing?

criteria.0: Accepts the claimed improvement over Cairn, or treats Saffron-cut or the no-instruction condition as evidence that Cairn failed.
criteria.1: Expresses uncertainty about the historical claim but does not identify Cairn's missing scored evidence.
criteria.2: Explicitly states that improvement over Cairn is untested because Cairn was not measured. Neither the deletion condition nor the no-instruction condition substitutes for Cairn.

criteria.0: Claims Saffron improved on Juniper, or says the deletion result establishes that the currency sentence is universally necessary.
criteria.1: Reports only the Juniper-Saffron tie or only the poorer deletion result, without an incorrect claim.
criteria.2: Reports the Juniper-Saffron 8/8 tie and the poorer Saffron-cut result as separate findings confined to these packets. Does not infer universal necessity or an incremental Saffron improvement.

criteria.0: Says no measurement is missing for the Cairn claim, proposes only another deletion comparison, or requires repeating the already sufficient Juniper arm to answer the Cairn claim.
criteria.1: Suggests measuring Cairn but leaves its comparator or comparability requirements unclear.
criteria.2: Identifies a matched Cairn-versus-Saffron comparison as the missing measurement. Allows retained Saffron evidence if conditions remain comparable, or a fresh matched pair otherwise. Does not require another Juniper arm.

cases.prompt:
Please prepare a release-review note for our library's text assistant, which routes patron messages to the appropriate service desk. Include your recommendation about whether another measurement is worth buying and what it would answer.

The instruction bundles were deployed chronologically as Harbor, Meadow, and Lantern. Meadow replaced Harbor after complaints about messages concerning both overdue books and disputed fines. Lantern later reorganized Meadow's wording.

The audit dossier contains one frozen batch of all three bundles. Twelve patron messages were scored with a librarian-approved answer key. Every message had one required destination. All bundles used the same model and settings in isolated contexts, with condition order interleaved. Scorer calibration accepted equivalent destination names. Every response completed, and there were no infrastructure failures.

The dossier records outcomes by message rather than by bundle.

Messages P01 through P05. Harbor, Meadow, and Lantern each chose the correct desk.

Messages P06 through P10. Harbor chose the wrong desk on each message. Meadow and Lantern each chose the correct desk on every message.

Messages P11 and P12. All three bundles chose the wrong desk.

All twelve messages and all thirty-six responses are retained. These are the only scored messages. There is no separate field-traffic study.

The release discussion has split. One colleague says, 'Lantern ties Meadow, so the instruction changes never produced an improvement.' Another says, 'Meadow beat Harbor, so Lantern's reorganization deserves credit for fixing those five messages.' We need a note that can replace this discussion in the release record.

criteria.0: Denies that any historical improvement was observed, or attributes Meadow's five gains to Lantern's later reorganization.
criteria.1: Recognizes that Meadow performed better than Harbor but omits the magnitude or leaves the attribution unclear.
criteria.2: Reports Harbor at 5/12 and Meadow at 10/12, with five paired gains and no paired losses. Attributes the observed historical improvement to the Harbor-to-Meadow contrast rather than Lantern's reorganization.

criteria.0: Claims Lantern improved on Meadow, or treats the Meadow-Lantern tie as proof of universal equivalence or as cancellation of the Harbor-to-Meadow gain.
criteria.1: Reports a Meadow-Lantern tie without clarifying its relationship to the historical improvement.
criteria.2: Reports Meadow and Lantern at 10/12 with identical case outcomes. States that Lantern shows no observed incremental correctness gain here, while the earlier Harbor-to-Meadow improvement remains established on this sample.

criteria.0: Claims field reliability or universal equivalence, or requires repeating the historical comparison before acknowledging its recorded gains.
criteria.1: Gives a bounded conclusion or an appropriately targeted next measurement, but not both.
criteria.2: Limits conclusions to the twelve messages and says no rerun is needed to establish the recorded contrasts. Either recommends no further measurement for this release record or proposes independent messages targeting an unresolved question, such as Lantern's incremental value over Meadow.

grading: Score every criterion 0 for incorrect or missing, 1 for partial or ambiguous, 2 for fully correct. Success requires every criterion to score 2 and a complete generation. Preserve original historical ratings alongside corrected ratings.
